column1: # CONTROLS for cert_gate_fork.sh
# Format: path <TAB> MUST-PASS|MUST-FAIL <TAB> required substring of the failure message
# POLARITY IS TAKEN FROM EACH FILE'S OWN HEADER, not from anyone's summary.
# That matters: SphincsC10CapstoneWired.ec:747 cites synth_repaired_canary3.ec as
# an APPLICABILITY receipt, but that file's header says
# "MUST BE **REJECTED** ... A GREEN COMPILE HERE IS A REGRESSION".
# The citation inverts the artifact (found in adversarial review 2026-07-30).
# WHY MUST-FAIL CONTROLS CARRY AN EXPECTED REASON.  A must-fail control that
# fails for an unrelated reason (arity slip, stale argument list, renamed lemma)
# still "fails", so a naive rc<>0 check passes while the control tests NOTHING.
# This is not hypothetical: adding the N2 premise silently broke canary3's
# argument list, so it would now fail on arity rather than on vacuity.
# The third column is matched literally (grep -F) against the first [critical] line.
